name: Kijjun
title: The Star God Worshipped by Israel
summary: Kijjun (also known as Kewan or Chiun) is the name of a star god that the Israelites worshipped during their apostasy. The god is mentioned in the book of the prophet Amos as an example of Israel's idolatry, and the reference is repeated by Stephen in Acts. Kijjun represents the astral idolatry that led to God's judgment upon Israel.

keyEvents.title: Amos' Accusation Against Israel's Idolatry
keyEvents.description: The prophet Amos accuses the Israelites of carrying with them Kijjun, their star god, through the wilderness and throughout their history as an expression of persistent idolatry.

keyEvents.title: Judgment Upon Israel for Idolatry
keyEvents.description: Amos proclaims that God will send Israel into exile because they have worshipped foreign gods, including Kijjun, instead of seeking the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Amos' Call to Repentance
keyEvents.description: In the context of condemning the worship of Kijjun, Amos calls the people to seek good and not evil, so that the Lord may be with them.

keyEvents.title: Stephen Quotes Amos Regarding Kijjun
keyEvents.description: In his speech before the Sanhedrin, Stephen quotes the prophet Amos and mentions the Israelites' worship of Kijjun as evidence of the people's repeated apostasy throughout history.

keyEvents.title: Stephen's Review of Israel's History of Apostasy
keyEvents.description: Stephen uses the reference to Kijjun as part of a broader review of how Israel repeatedly turned away from God, which ultimately led to his martyrdom.
